name: Ice Halo
desc: The sky doing optics with itself — countless hexagonal ice prisms drifting in cirrus each bend the light through their 60-degree faces and pile it up at the angle of minimum deviation, printing a 22-degree ring around the sun with red hard against the inside, a fainter 46-degree ring beyond it, a pair of burning sun dogs either side, a specular pillar shivering up through the sun off tumbling plate crystals, and an upturned circumzenithal bow of the purest colour in the sky. Purely additive, so it lies over a scene as light rather than paint.

energy.doc: brightness of the whole display and the sparkle of the diamond dust (master knob)

scale.doc: angular scale of the sky — sets how big 22 degrees is on the frame

density.doc: ice-crystal population: sharpens the rings, brings in the 46-degree halo, the dogs and the diamond dust

speed.doc: cirrus drift, crystal scintillation and twinkle rate

hue.doc: colour cast over the true dispersion (205 = neutral daylight; the spectral order red-inside is preserved)

y.doc: sun position y — low in frame leaves room for the upper arcs

arcs.doc: which of the display is showing; 'full' is everything, the rest isolate one component

style.doc: aesthetic: cold daylight, a dim blue lunar halo, exaggerated colour, a dispersion-free silver display, or an orange sodium-lit urban night

seed.doc: seed — drift phases, crystal patchiness, diamond-dust placement

alpha.doc: layer opacity — defaults below full so it sits politely over a live scene
